messages.subject: ACI - Window Length
parts:
Hi All

I am quite new to bioacoustics and have been playing with acoustic indices. With ACI I have been getting mixed and obscure results, and I was told that changes to the window length may help. I am curious about the best way to determine the most appropriate window length when running the script. I understand that the window length essentially changes the resolution of the spectrogram, off of which the ACI is calculated. I looked at my recordings visually and played around with the spectral displays to find a window length that appeared to show individual bird calls most clearly without blurring them out or chopping them up. I then used that as the window length in R for ACI. Does this sound like a reasonable approach and does anyone have advice on determining the best window length to use? Has anyone else noticed significant changes in the outcomes with changes to window length?

Thank you!

Laura

messages.author: 4271370c9274971b
messages.subject: Re: ACI - Window Length
parts:
Laura,

With regard to choosing the best window settings, I've been told to use the window length/overlap that allows you to best pick out the information you're interested in, and then stay consistent with them. The Pieretti et al. 2008 paper uses a window length of 512 points, so it might be best to stick with the default setting for the ACI function.

Here's a resource that helped me conceptualize the process. I'm not an expert, so it might require some digging in the literature to see what other people have already done. 

Sean
